NASB.1: Then Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam sang on that day, saying,
NASB.2: 'That the leaders led in Israel, That the people volunteered, Bless the LORD!
NASB.3: 'Hear, O kings; give ear, O rulers! I-- to the LORD, I will sing, I will sing praise to the LORD, the God of Israel.
NASB.4: 'LORD, when You went out from Seir, When You marched from the field of Edom, The earth quaked, the heavens also dripped, Even the clouds dripped water.
NASB.5: 'The mountains quaked at the presence of the LORD, This Sinai, at the presence of the LORD, the God of Israel.
NASB.6: 'In the days of Shamgar the son of Anath, In the days of Jael, the highways were deserted, And travelers went by roundabout ways.
NASB.7: 'The peasantry ceased, they ceased in Israel, Until I, Deborah, arose, Until I arose, a mother in Israel.
NASB.8: 'New gods were chosen; Then war [was] in the gates. Not a shield or a spear was seen Among forty thousand in Israel.
NASB.9: 'My heart [goes out] to the commanders of Israel, The volunteers among the people; Bless the LORD!
NASB.10: 'You who ride on white donkeys, You who sit on [rich] carpets, And you who travel on the road-- sing!
NASB.11: 'At the sound of those who divide [flocks] among the watering places, There they shall recount the righteous deeds of the LORD, The righteous deeds for His peasantry in Israel. Then the people of the LORD went down to the gates.
NASB.12: 'Awake, awake, Deborah; Awake, awake, sing a song! Arise, Barak, and take away your captives, O son of Abinoam.
NASB.13: 'Then survivors came down to the nobles; The people of the LORD came down to me as warriors.
NASB.14: 'From Ephraim those whose root is in Amalek [came down], Following you, Benjamin, with your peoples; From Machir commanders came down, And from Zebulun those who wield the staff of office.
NASB.15: 'And the princes of Issachar [were] with Deborah; As [was] Issachar, so [was] Barak; Into the valley they rushed at his heels; Among the divisions of Reuben [There were] great resolves of heart.
NASB.16: 'Why did you sit among the sheepfolds, To hear the piping for the flocks? Among the divisions of Reuben [There were] great searchings of heart.
NASB.17: 'Gilead remained across the Jordan; And why did Dan stay in ships? Asher sat at the seashore, And remained by its landings.
NASB.18: 'Zebulun [was] a people who despised their lives [even] to death, And Naphtali also, on the high places of the field.
NASB.19: 'The kings came [and] fought; Then fought the kings of Canaan At Taanach near the waters of Megiddo; They took no plunder in silver.
NASB.20: 'The stars fought from heaven, From their courses they fought against Sisera.
NASB.21: 'The torrent of Kishon swept them away, The ancient torrent, the torrent Kishon. O my soul, march on with strength.
NASB.22: 'Then the horses' hoofs beat From the dashing, the dashing of his valiant steeds.
NASB.23: 'Curse Meroz,' said the angel of the LORD, 'Utterly curse its inhabitants; Because they did not come to the help of the LORD, To the help of the LORD against the warriors.'
NASB.24: 'Most blessed of women is Jael, The wife of Heber the Kenite; Most blessed is she of women in the tent.
NASB.25: 'He asked for water [and] she gave him milk; In a magnificent bowl she brought him curds.
NASB.26: 'She reached out her hand for the tent peg, And her right hand for the workmen's hammer. Then she struck Sisera, she smashed his head; And she shattered and pierced his temple.
NASB.27: 'Between her feet he bowed, he fell, he lay; Between her feet he bowed, he fell; Where he bowed, there he fell dead.
NASB.28: 'Out of the window she looked and lamented, The mother of Sisera through the lattice, 'Why does his chariot delay in coming? Why do the hoofbeats of his chariots tarry?'
NASB.29: 'Her wise princesses would answer her, Indeed she repeats her words to herself,
NASB.30: 'Are they not finding, are they not dividing the spoil? A maiden, two maidens for every warrior; To Sisera a spoil of dyed work, A spoil of dyed work embroidered, Dyed work of double embroidery on the neck of the spoiler?'
NASB.31: 'Thus let all Your enemies perish, O LORD; But let those who love Him be like the rising of the sun in its might.' And the land was undisturbed for forty years.

NKJV.1: Then Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam sang on that day, saying:
NKJV.2: “When leaders lead in Israel,  When the people willingly offer themselves, Bless the LORD!
NKJV.3: “Hear, O kings! Give ear, O princes! I, even I, will sing to the LORD; I will sing praise to the LORD God of Israel.
NKJV.4: “LORD, when You went out from Seir, When You marched from the field of Edom, The earth trembled and the heavens poured, The clouds also poured water;
NKJV.5: The mountains gushed before the LORD,  This Sinai, before the LORD God of Israel.
NKJV.6: “In the days of Shamgar, son of Anath, In the days of Jael,  The highways were deserted, And the travelers walked along the byways.
NKJV.7: Village life ceased, it ceased in Israel, Until I, Deborah, arose, Arose a mother in Israel.
NKJV.8: They chose new gods; Then there was war in the gates; Not a shield or spear was seen among forty thousand in Israel.
NKJV.9: My heart is with the rulers of Israel Who offered themselves willingly with the people. Bless the LORD!
NKJV.10: “Speak, you who ride on white donkeys, Who sit in judges’ attire, And who walk along the road.
NKJV.11: Far from the noise of the archers, among the watering places, There they shall recount the righteous acts of the LORD, The righteous acts for His villagers in Israel; Then the people of the LORD shall go down to the gates.
NKJV.12: “Awake,  awake, Deborah! Awake, awake, sing a song! Arise, Barak, and lead your captives away, O son of Abinoam!
NKJV.13: “Then the survivors came down, the people against the nobles; The LORD came down for me against the mighty.
NKJV.14: From Ephraim were those whose roots were in Amalek. After you, Benjamin, with your peoples, From Machir rulers came down, And from Zebulun those who bear the recruiter’s staff.
NKJV.15: And the princes of Issachar were with Deborah; As Issachar, so was Barak Sent into the valley under his command; Among the divisions of Reuben There were great resolves of heart.
NKJV.16: Why did you sit among the sheepfolds, To hear the pipings for the flocks? The divisions of Reuben have great searchings of heart.
NKJV.17: Gilead stayed beyond the Jordan, And why did Dan remain on ships?  Asher continued at the seashore, And stayed by his inlets.
NKJV.18: Zebulun is a people who jeopardized their lives to the point of death, Naphtali also, on the heights of the battlefield.
NKJV.19: “The kings came and fought, Then the kings of Canaan fought In Taanach, by the waters of Megiddo; They took no spoils of silver.
NKJV.20: They fought from the heavens; The stars from their courses fought against Sisera.
NKJV.21: The torrent of Kishon swept them away, That ancient torrent, the torrent of Kishon. O my soul, march on in strength!
NKJV.22: Then the horses’ hooves pounded, The galloping, galloping of his steeds.
NKJV.23: ‘Curse Meroz,’ said the angel of the LORD, ‘Curse its inhabitants bitterly, Because they did not come to the help of the LORD, To the help of the LORD against the mighty.’
NKJV.24: “Most blessed among women is Jael, The wife of Heber the Kenite;  Blessed is she among women in tents.
NKJV.25: He asked for water, she gave milk; She brought out cream in a lordly bowl.
NKJV.26: She stretched her hand to the tent peg, Her right hand to the workmen’s hammer; She pounded Sisera, she pierced his head, She split and struck through his temple.
NKJV.27: At her feet he sank, he fell, he lay still; At her feet he sank, he fell; Where he sank, there he fell dead.
NKJV.28: “The mother of Sisera looked through the window, And cried out through the lattice, ‘Why is his chariot so long in coming? Why tarries the clatter of his chariots?’
NKJV.29: Her wisest ladies answered her, Yes, she answered herself,
NKJV.30: ‘Are they not finding and dividing the spoil: To every man a girl or two; For Sisera, plunder of dyed garments, Plunder of garments embroidered and dyed, Two pieces of dyed embroidery for the neck of the looter?’
NKJV.31: “Thus let all Your enemies perish, O LORD! But let those who love Him be like the sun When it comes out in full strength.” So the land had rest for forty years.

ESV.1: Then sang Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam on that day:
ESV.2: “That the leaders took the lead in Israel, that the people offered themselves willingly, bless the LORD!
ESV.3: “Hear, O kings; give ear, O princes; to the LORD I will sing; I will make melody to the LORD, the God of Israel.
ESV.4: “LORD, when you went out from Seir, when you marched from the region of Edom, the earth trembled and the heavens dropped, yes, the clouds dropped water.
ESV.5: The mountains quaked before the LORD, even Sinai before the LORD,  the God of Israel.
ESV.6: “In the days of Shamgar, son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways were abandoned, and travelers kept to the byways.
ESV.7: The villagers ceased in Israel; they ceased to be until I arose; I, Deborah, arose as a mother in Israel.
ESV.8: When new gods were chosen, then war was in the gates. Was shield or spear to be seen among forty thousand in Israel?
ESV.9: My heart goes out to the commanders of Israel who offered themselves willingly among the people. Bless the LORD.
ESV.10: “Tell of it, you who ride on white donkeys, you who sit on rich carpets  and you who walk by the way.
ESV.11: To the sound of musicians  at the watering places, there they repeat the righteous triumphs of the LORD, the righteous triumphs of his villagers in Israel.  “Then down to the gates marched the people of the LORD.
ESV.12: “Awake, awake, Deborah! Awake, awake, break out in a song! Arise, Barak, lead away your captives, O son of Abinoam.
ESV.13: Then down marched the remnant of the noble; the people of the LORD marched down for me against the mighty.
ESV.14: From Ephraim their root they marched down into the valley,  following you, Benjamin, with your kinsmen; from Machir marched down the commanders, and from Zebulun those who bear the lieutenant's  staff;
ESV.15: the princes of Issachar came with Deborah, and Issachar faithful to Barak; into the valley they rushed at his heels. Among the clans of Reuben there were great searchings of heart.
ESV.16: Why did you sit still among the sheepfolds, to hear the whistling for the flocks? Among the clans of Reuben there were great searchings of heart.
ESV.17: Gilead stayed beyond the Jordan; and Dan, why did he stay with the ships? Asher sat still at the coast of the sea, staying by his landings.
ESV.18: Zebulun is a people who risked their lives to the death; Naphtali, too, on the heights of the field.
ESV.19: “The kings came, they fought; then fought the kings of Canaan, at Taanach, by the waters of Megiddo; they got no spoils of silver.
ESV.20: From heaven the stars fought, from their courses they fought against Sisera.
ESV.21: The torrent Kishon swept them away, the ancient torrent, the torrent Kishon. March on, my soul, with might!
ESV.22: “Then loud beat the horses' hoofs with the galloping, galloping of his steeds.
ESV.23: “Curse Meroz, says the angel of the LORD, curse its inhabitants thoroughly, because they did not come to the help of the LORD, to the help of the LORD against the mighty.
ESV.24: “Most blessed of women be Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, of tent-dwelling women most blessed.
ESV.25: He asked for water and she gave him milk; she brought him curds in a noble's bowl.
ESV.26: She sent her hand to the tent peg and her right hand to the workmen's mallet; she struck Sisera; she crushed his head; she shattered and pierced his temple.
ESV.27: Between her feet he sank, he fell, he lay still; between her feet he sank, he fell; where he sank, there he fell — dead.
ESV.28: “Out of the window she peered, the mother of Sisera wailed through the lattice: ‘Why is his chariot so long in coming? Why tarry the hoofbeats of his chariots?’
ESV.29: Her wisest princesses answer, indeed, she answers herself,
ESV.30: ‘Have they not found and divided the spoil? — A womb or two for every man; spoil of dyed materials for Sisera, spoil of dyed materials embroidered, two pieces of dyed work embroidered for the neck as spoil?’
ESV.31: “So may all your enemies perish, O LORD! But your friends be like the sun as he rises in his might.”  And the land had rest for forty years.

NLT.1: On that day Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam sang this song:
NLT.2:
“Israel’s leaders took charge,
and the people gladly followed.
Praise the LORD!
NLT.3:
“Listen, you kings!
Pay attention, you mighty rulers!
For I will sing to the LORD.
I will make music to the LORD, the God of Israel.
NLT.4:
“LORD, when you set out from Seir
and marched across the fields of Edom,
the earth trembled,
and the cloudy skies poured down rain.
NLT.5:
The mountains quaked in the presence of the LORD,
the God of Mount Sinai —
in the presence of the LORD,
the God of Israel.
NLT.6:
“In the days of Shamgar son of Anath,
and in the days of Jael,
people avoided the main roads,
and travelers stayed on winding pathways.
NLT.7:
There were few people left in the villages of Israel —
until Deborah arose as a mother for Israel.
NLT.8:
When Israel chose new gods,
war erupted at the city gates.
Yet not a shield or spear could be seen
among forty thousand warriors in Israel!
NLT.9:
My heart is with the commanders of Israel,
with those who volunteered for war.
Praise the LORD!
NLT.10:
“Consider this, you who ride on fine donkeys,
you who sit on fancy saddle blankets,
and you who walk along the road.
NLT.11:
Listen to the village musicians
gathered at the watering holes.
They recount the righteous victories of the LORD
and the victories of his villagers in Israel.
Then the people of the LORD
marched down to the city gates.
NLT.12:
“Wake up, Deborah, wake up!
Wake up, wake up, and sing a song!
Arise, Barak!
Lead your captives away, son of Abinoam!
NLT.13:
“Down from Tabor marched the few against the nobles.
The people of the LORD marched down against mighty warriors.
NLT.14:
They came down from Ephraim —
a land that once belonged to the Amalekites;
they followed you, Benjamin, with your troops.
From Makir the commanders marched down;
from Zebulun came those who carry a commander’s staff.
NLT.15:
The princes of Issachar were with Deborah and Barak.
They followed Barak, rushing into the valley.
But in the tribe of Reuben
there was great indecision.
NLT.16:
Why did you sit at home among the sheepfolds —
to hear the shepherds whistle for their flocks?
Yes, in the tribe of Reuben
there was great indecision.
NLT.17:
Gilead remained east of the Jordan.
And why did Dan stay home?
Asher sat unmoved at the seashore,
remaining in his harbors.
NLT.18:
But Zebulun risked his life,
as did Naphtali, on the heights of the battlefield.
NLT.19:
“The kings of Canaan came and fought,
at Taanach near Megiddo’s springs,
but they carried off no silver treasures.
NLT.20:
The stars fought from heaven.
The stars in their orbits fought against Sisera.
NLT.21:
The Kishon River swept them away —
that ancient torrent, the Kishon.
March on with courage, my soul!
NLT.22:
Then the horses’ hooves hammered the ground,
the galloping, galloping of Sisera’s mighty steeds.
NLT.23:
‘Let the people of Meroz be cursed,’ said the angel of the LORD.
‘Let them be utterly cursed,
because they did not come to help the LORD —
to help the LORD against the mighty warriors.’
NLT.24:
“Most blessed among women is Jael,
the wife of Heber the Kenite.
May she be blessed above all women who live in tents.
NLT.25:
Sisera asked for water,
and she gave him milk.
In a bowl fit for nobles,
she brought him yogurt.
NLT.26:
Then with her left hand she reached for a tent peg,
and with her right hand for the workman’s hammer.
She struck Sisera with the hammer, crushing his head.
With a shattering blow, she pierced his temples.
NLT.27:
He sank, he fell,
he lay still at her feet.
And where he sank,
there he died.
NLT.28:
“From the window Sisera’s mother looked out.
Through the window she watched for his return, saying,
‘Why is his chariot so long in coming?
Why don’t we hear the sound of chariot wheels?’
NLT.29:
“Her wise women answer,
and she repeats these words to herself:
NLT.30:
‘They must be dividing the captured plunder —
with a woman or two for every man.
There will be colorful robes for Sisera,
and colorful, embroidered robes for me.
Yes, the plunder will include
colorful robes embroidered on both sides.’
NLT.31:
“LORD, may all your enemies die like Sisera!
But may those who love you rise like the sun in all its power!”
Then there was peace in the land for forty years.
